messages:
incident-bot: realtime alert: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/generate (model=rw-13b-prod) in prod-us-east. p99=3.1s (SLO 1.0s). paging @carlos (primary oncall) and @maria. alert dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/4987659900 :rotating_light:

carlos: ack. joining. pattern: sustained tail for ~8m. any signs of error increases or just stalls?

incident-bot: error rate stable (~0.4%). streaming chunk gaps elevated; #streams with >5s gap went from 2 -> 120 in the window. Hot hosts: serving-us-east-5 nodes 12/13/14. Canary deploy to rw-13b-prod at 15:02 UTC preceded the spike.

maria: pausing canary immediately. marking deploy as potential cause. @devon can you pull runtime trace and queue depth for the affected hosts?

devon: grabbing traces. early findings: long shard scheduling delays and token emit backlog. sample runtime log: 
```
[2026-03-15T15:08:34Z] runtime: emit_delay_ms=1820 shard=12 reason="io_wait"
[2026-03-15T15:08:34Z] runtime: kv_cache_hit=false key=prefix_abc
[2026-03-15T15:08:35Z] runtime: batch_size=1 enqueue_delay_ms=260
```
NVMe read latency also shows tail spikes on node serving-us-east-5-12.

rachel: infra-bot reports EBS I/O throttling events around same timeframe on those hosts. opening INFRA-2302 to track.

infra-bot: INFRA-2302 created: Investigate EBS throttling on serving-us-east-5-12..-14. linked nodes set to maintenance flag=false yet.

carlos: quick mitigation plan: 1) stop canary (done) 2) reduce weight to affected hosts via routing override 3) enable temporary model fallback to rw-6b-quant for non-SLA tenants with >1s estimated latency 4) increase chunk timeout heuristics on streaming to avoid stalls. Maria take routing, Devon take runtime fallback, Rachel owns infra ticket and node isolation.

maria: executing routing override: 
```bash
rdwctl routing set --route "/v1/generate" --exclude-hosts serving-us-east-5-12,serving-us-east-5-13,serving-us-east-5-14 --preferred-pools serving-us-east-6,eu-west-2 --apply
```
applied, traffic shifting.

devon: applying runtime fallback rule and bumping stream chunk timeout to 6s to tolerate transient IO. rule: 
```yaml
# runtime override
when: estimated_emit_delay_ms > 1000 and tenant_tier != premium
then: model = rw-6b-quant
```
rolled out to routing layer as a non-disruptive runtime override.

support-bot: Noted 3 enterprise reports from 15:10-15:12 UTC mentioning long responses and truncated streams. Ticket IDs: SUP-7820, SUP-7821, SUP-7822.

carlos: customer impact: roughly 0.8% of requests in the window impacted with >2s tail. severity set to Sev2 given enterprise reports and partial recovery risk. cadence set to 10m.

incident-bot: telemetry update (15:15 UTC): p95=610ms, p99=1.6s, streams with >5s gap down to 18, EBS throttling events still present but decreasing.

rachel: INFRA-2302 notes: host serving-us-east-5-12 shows high devstat stalls on NVMe controller, possibly noisy neighbor. long-term remediation: move disks to different EBS pool and investigate placement. marking hosts 12-14 for drain.

maria: routing change shows p95 improving to 420ms within 90s. p99 still elevated but trending down. I'm monitoring connection handoffs to ensure no request loss.

devon: runtime logs show KV cache miss burst coincident with IO stalls; increased miss-rate caused more work per request and smaller batches -> tail blowup. applied a soft admission control to prefer batching for small requests while fallback active.

incident-bot: 15:20 UTC snapshot: p95=390ms, p99=1.05s, kv_miss_rate back to baseline for routed hosts. remaining p99 tail comes mainly from requests pinned to draining hosts (12-14).

carlos: mark hosts 12-14 as unhealthy; start draining, cordon nodes. Rachel proceed with drain plan. Also ask placement team about EBS IOPS limits for that AZ.

rachel: cordon and drain initiated. nodes will complete in ~3-5m as active streams finish; we'll force-terminate after grace if necessary. creating follow-up INFRA task to request EBS limit increase or move.

support-bot: Customer AcmeCorp (SUP-7820) updated with mitigation steps and ETA for full recovery. they requested a post-incident timeline.

devon: enabling extended tracing on the drained hosts to collect full token timelines (14:55-15:25s window). pushing traces to s3://redwood-telemetry/incidents/4987659900/traces.zip

incident-bot: final update (15:26 UTC): p95=340ms, p99=0.95s, streams with >5s gaps=3, node-level IO errors falling. marking incident mitigated, continue watch for 45m.

carlos: closing active paging. action items: 1) Infra: replace or reprovision EBS on hosts 12-14 + validate placement (rachel) 2) Runtime: add stronger canary gating for storage IO metrics before model canary promotion (devon) 3) Routing: improve traffic shift fallback to avoid draining single AZ (maria) 4) Support: provide customer timeline and impact calc (support-bot / rachel). Assigning owners and due dates in INFRA-2302/RT-998/RT-999.

rachel: evidence bundle uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/4987659900/evidence.tar.gz containing dashboards, node metrics, traces.

incident-bot: incident closed (15:28 UTC) - monitoring continue. reopen if p99 > 1s or >0.5% requests impacted.

carlos: thanks all. postmortem owner: Devon. target draft due EOD tomorrow.
